newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya central bank calls for calm, intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Kenya central bank calls for calm, intervenes.

text.p: Kenya's central bank called for an end to panic on Nairobi's foreign exchange market on Wednesday and intervened to stem the shilling's slide by selling dollars.
Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem urged the foreign exchange market to trade "in an orderly manner so that losses arising from the panic and speculative transactions would be minimised".
Commercial bank dealers said following his statement the Central Bank intervened, selling at least $10 million.
"The shilling exchange rate to the U.S. dollar opened at a mean rate of 64 and rapidly depreciated to a selling rate as low as 69...the speed of depreciation is worrying," Cheserem said.

He said commercial banks reported that several importers were rushing to pay their foreign bills in order to minimise exchange losses while exporters were holding back dollars in anticipation of further shilling losses.

In a statement, Cheserem also said foreign investors in government treasury bills and stocks were in the market after the IMF halted a key loan package to Kenya on Thursday, buying foreign exchange to repatriate their investments.
